title: The Analog and Power Squeeze: TI, ADI, onsemi, ST, and Renesas Raise Prices
body_markdown:
TI's latest notice, dated September 1, gave no effective date and[set no uniform increase](https://www.trendforce.com/news/?p=63900) , since adjustments vary by material, technology, and process.[ADI said](https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/13/news-adi-reportedly-set-to-raise-prices-again-on-september-with-military-chips-facing-up-to-30-hike/) it will reinvest all of the added revenue in its own fabs and test capacity to ease lead times of up to six months. The Renesas increase applies to orders already on hand that ship on or after January 1, unless agreed otherwise in writing.


## Why everyday parts are caught in it


Most power management chips and power discretes still run on 8-inch wafers. Average utilization at the top ten foundries' 8-inch fabs reached 88% this year and is[expected to hit 90%](https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260630-13127.html) in the second half, as TSMC and Samsung cut capacity and the industry prepares a third round of foundry price increases running into 2027.
‍


AI is claiming a growing share of that capacity. AI servers need far higher power density, so suppliers prioritize them, and TrendForce expected PMIC lead times for general-purpose servers to[stretch from 21 to 26 weeks to 35 to 40](https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260415-13013.html) . Our sourcing team is hearing the same from suppliers: the tightest TI and ADI categories are the ones going into AI servers. In the independent channel, some ADI precision amplifier, converter, and voltage reference families now quote 60 to 70 weeks.
‍


Buyers have noticed. In a[UBS survey](https://www.techflowpost.com/en-US/article/34680) published October 16, 76% of direct buyers and 70% of distributors said they were concerned about shortages over the next six months, and distributor inventories of power analog parts fell 10% in the third quarter. In August, 64% of electronics manufacturers told the[Global Electronics Association](https://www.electronics.org/blog/supply-chain-tightening-again-data-makes-it-hard-look-away) that components were available only in limited quantities or with extended lead times, and none described supply as readily available.


## What this means right now


The shift shows up on the Mobius marketplace. These five manufacturers went from about one in eight RFQs between late April and mid-July to nearly one in three over the past three months. Texas Instruments alone went from 2% of RFQs to 15%. Two-thirds of TI requests were for power management parts, mostly step-down regulators, with precision analog and sensor parts making up the rest. Only a little over half of all requests for these five suppliers drew a quote.
